:::{#exm-logistic-slope}

#### The slope of a logistic probability curve

Suppose
$\alpha = -2$ and $\beta = 0.5$ in the single-predictor logistic regression model of @eq-unipredictor-logreg.
The code below approximates $\derivf{\pi}{x}$ at $x = 1$ with a central difference,
and compares it with the formula of @cor-logistic-slope:

```{r}
#| label: exm-logistic-slope-calc
#| code-fold: show
ex_alpha <- -2
ex_beta <- 0.5
ex_pi <- function(x) plogis(ex_alpha + ex_beta * x)
ex_h <- 1e-6
ex_numeric <- (ex_pi(1 + ex_h) - ex_pi(1 - ex_h)) / (2 * ex_h)
ex_formula <- ex_pi(1) * (1 - ex_pi(1)) * ex_beta
```

At $x = 1$, $\pi =$ `r round(ex_pi(1), 4)`.
The central difference gives `r round(ex_numeric, 5)`
and the formula $\pi(1-\pi)\beta$ gives `r round(ex_formula, 5)`,
so the two agree.

:::
